title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
lede: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes perplexity, a measure of how well a model predicts the next token, as the shared yardstick labs could use to cap AI development.

points: The post follows Dario Amodei's plan to pace the frontier, which called for common safety standards and limits on the rate of AI progress.
Pachocki argues that capability benchmarks go stale quickly as models improve, while perplexity keeps telling you something.
His chart shows perplexity falling across OpenAI models since GPT-3.5, with GPT-4 near 0.91.
He ties losses below 0.8 to the arrival of transformative capabilities in cybersecurity and mathematics.
Under the proposal, labs would not pass an agreed threshold until monitoring and understanding of AI behaviour reach a concrete milestone.

sections.text: If labs adopted it, limits would attach to a training metric every lab already tracks, rather than to task benchmarks that keep being outgrown.
